historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Al-Sham. The Conquest of Syria, E.J. Costello, Translation for the Medieval Texts Series, 1993, p. 198.
historical_references.context: Ashaj ibn Rabi'ah was the leader of an Arab tribe, Banu Kalb, in the Syrian province of Jazirah. He saw the Muslim army led by Khalid ibn al-Walid approaching his territory, and sent a delegation to negotiate peace. When the Muslims refused, Ashaj prepared his forces, and the Battle of Marj Rahit (634 AD) took place. Ashaj was killed in the battle.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri, Ansab al-Ashraf, Translated by P.K. Hitti, 1924, p. 257. The name Ashaj carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ashaj ibn Rabi'ah was a powerful Arab chieftain, ruling over the tribes in Jazirah. He was an ally of the Byzantines and resisted the Muslim penetration into the region. However, when he saw the might of the Muslim army, he tried to negotiate peace. The negotiations failed, and Ashaj led his forces against the Muslims. The Battle of Marj Rahit took place, and Ashaj was killed.
